sections.title: Education
sections.lead: Learn about the different kinds of education offered at SIDE.

sections.title: A unique, holistic approach to learning.
sections.text: SIDE offers a number of different learning pathways to both primary and secondary students, offering access to a complete education from Kindergarten all the way through Year 12, whether you're learning at home, on the road, or in a classroom.
sections.caption: All you need to do is pick what works best for you.

sections.title: How It Works

tools.name: Moodle
tools.body: Our online learning hub, where students reach lessons, assignments and resources from anywhere in the world.
points: Access lessons and resources from anywhere

tools.name: Webex
tools.body: Our secure video conferencing tool for live classes, meetings and catch-ups with teachers.
points: Ask questions and share your screen
Collaborate with classmates as at a traditional school

tools.name: In Person
tools.body: Teachers love stepping out from behind the screen to visit their rural classes.
points: Teachers visit rural classes in person
Familiar online smiles become tangible, strengthening connections

sections.waysTitle: Two ways to join the class

ways.tag: At home or on the road
ways.title: At Home and on the Road
ways.body: Outside of a traditional school setting, students use their webcam to attend livestreamed classes - talking with their teacher and classmates via microphone and text chat, collaborating on group projects through shared documents and participating in class activities just as they would in person.

ways.title: In Class at School
ways.body: In classrooms, we implement a large display and video-conferencing setup, allowing students the ability to interact with their online teacher and classmates as if they were in the same room. This is supported by an on-site supervisor who is there to ensure the safety and wellbeing of students.

sections.title: Primary & Secondary Pathways

blocks.text: Students can access a full-curriculum right from their home, wherever that might be.

items.title: Travelling temporarily
items.text: The student needs to be travelling for a minimum enrolment period of one school semester, or 20 school weeks.

items.title: Geographically isolated
items.text: The student needs to demonstrate that they are geographically isolated in WA as defined by at least one of the categories below:

items.title: Referral
items.text: Some students have special circumstances that afford them some extra allowances as to which programs they can access.

blocks.text: Schools can supplement their education offerings to fill areas of need.

items.title: Scheduling
items.text: Sometimes students can't attend classes during standard hours due to personal circumstances. We provide the flexibility to learn outside regular school times to accommodate individual needs.

items.title: Transfers
items.text: We support students who transfer mid-year by helping them continue their previous subjects without disruption. We also assist classes affected by teacher transitions, ensuring a smooth learning experience during these changes.

items.title: Specialised subjects
items.text: When schools don't have teachers with expertise in specific subjects, we step in to provide that specialised instruction. This ensures students can access courses they're passionate about, even if they're not available at their school.

sections.lead: SIDE’s subjects, courses, and programs are fully accredited by the School Curriculum and Standards Authority, offering students engaging and flexible learning in an online environment.

sections.title: Blended Pathway
sections.lead: The Blended pathway is available to Secondary students (Years 7–12) only, for students engaged in high intensity athletic or artistic pursuits.

items.title: Elite arts / sports
items.text: For students who demonstrate exceptional sporting or performing arts commitments which prevent them from attending mainstream school.

items.title: Dance
items.text: For students who demonstrate that they are enrolled in a full time registered ballet/dance school and unable to attend a mainstream school.

items.title: Recreational pursuits
items.text: For students involved in a club, organisation or association where opportunities are provided for the development of skills and knowledge.

sections.title: Key Documents
sections.lead: Important documents related to Primary and Secondary education.

sections.title: Our Culturally Responsive Education Program
sections.lead: The Regional and Remote Teaching Team (RRTT) delivers blended, culturally responsive programs to Aboriginal students in the Kimberley and Goldfields. Eight subject specialists co-develop context-specific programs reflecting community aspirations and needs.
sections.body:
In 2024, the Regional and Remote Teaching Team strengthened student wellbeing, engagement, and achievement through targeted, responsive teaching. They used curriculum-linked data to address learning gaps, worked closely with schools, families, and communities to ensure culturally relevant programs, and supported students with personalised plans, face-to-face visits, and flexible delivery.

Collaboration was embedded through regular team planning, while partnerships with training providers and local industries helped create clear pathways to further education and employment.

sections.title: English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EALD)
sections.lead: Building strong foundations for kids in Years 3-10 in English for confident communication and learning success.
sections.body:
The EALD Program supports students who mainly speak a language other than English. It provides targeted instruction in reading, writing, speaking, and listening to help learners build the language skills needed for everyday communication and academic study across all subjects.

Classes are structured to create a supportive learning environment where students can progress at their own pace. Through practical language use, cultural understanding, and ongoing assessment, the program prepares students to transition confidently into mainstream classes and participate fully in school life.
